title: Density Saturation and Autocorrelation Characteristics of Interlayer Exciton Ensembles in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ Heterostructures
authors: Mirco Troue, Johannes Figueiredo, Alina Scheuermann, Sebastian Loy, Jonas Kiemle, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Ursula Wurstbauer, Alexander W. Holleitner
abstract: We investigate interlayer excitons in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterostructures using time-resolved photoluminescence and second-order autocorrelation measurements across a wide range of excitation powers and bath temperatures. By analyzing the photoluminescence amplitude and lifetime of the interlayer exciton state with the lowest emission energy, we extract a corresponding density-temperature diagram. The extracted exciton density exhibits a saturation at approximately $10^{13}$cm$^{-2}$, consistent with values predicted for a Mott transition of interlayer exciton ensembles in van der Waals heterostructures. Moreover, possible interpretations beyond the Mott transition are discussed. We further test whether the density limit is accompanied by a departure from classical photon statistics. The second-order autocorrelation measurements reveal that the photoluminescence maintains an emission characteristic of $g^{(2)}(0) \approx 1$ from low exciton densities up to the maximum reachable density in the investigated exciton ensembles consistent with the lowest-energy exciton ensemble obeying Poissonian statistics.
summary: This work experimentally investigates interlayer excitons in $	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WSe}_2$ heterostructures, determining that the exciton density saturates at a value consistent with a Mott transition. Furthermore, the emission statistics are found to remain Poissonian ($g^{(2)}(0) \approx 1$) even at high densities, suggesting independent photon emission despite strong correlations.
main_problem: The study investigates the density saturation and the nature of photon emission statistics for interlayer exciton ensembles in $	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WSe}_2$ heterostructures.
main_result: The exciton density saturates at $\approx 10^{13} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$, consistent with a Mott transition, while the second-order autocorrelation function $g^{(2)}(0)$ remains near unity, indicating Poissonian statistics.
method: The research combines time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) measurements to extract exciton density and lifetime, with Hanbury Brown and Twiss (HBT) measurements to probe photon statistics.
model_or_system: The physical system is the interlayer exciton (IX) ensemble formed at the interface of $	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WSe}_2$ van-der-Waals heterostructures, which are studied under varying excitation powers and temperatures.
key_observables: Exciton density ($n_{	ext{ex}}$), PL lifetime, and the second-order autocorrelation function $g^{(2)}(0)$.
important_parameters: Saturation density ($\approx 10^{13} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$), bath temperature (down to $1.7 	ext{ K}$), and excitation power.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the density saturation is governed by a Mott transition, although photo-doping renormalization is also considered as an alternative mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate PL spectra, time-resolved decay curves, the dependence of PL lifetimes on temperature/power, and the measurement of $g^{(2)}(	au)$ confirming Poissonian statistics.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements across different excitation regimes, first determining the density-temperature diagram via PL analysis, then testing the statistical nature of the emission using HBT measurements, and finally discussing the implications of the observed saturation.
why_interesting: The combination of studying a Mott transition in an excitonic system alongside the measurement of photon statistics ($g^{(2)}$) provides a rich platform for understanding the crossover between classical, weakly interacting, and strongly correlated quantum many-body states.
